image.subject: a candle-lit 18th-century lodge room with a wooden table covered in open letters and a map, three empty chairs pulled up around it

storyboard.claim: The Illuminati ideal was a world joined by reason and free of gatekeepers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A candle-lit lodge room with letters and a map on the table, the old ideal of open reasoning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the closing argument on the internet's promise.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lodge room shows the original ideal the viewer is about to see betrayed.

image.subject: a crowded market street with stalls and jostling people pushing in every direction, seen from behind, no gate or barrier in sight

storyboard.claim: Instead of reason, the open network became chaotic and fast.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A packed street with no gate, people shoving in every direction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the ideal into the reality of the open network.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the absence of gatekeepers as a crowd with no barrier.

image.subject: a dark city square at dusk filled with thousands of people, a single phone screen glowing bright in the middle of the crowd, seen from behind

storyboard.claim: The internet became a battleground where viral contagion can upend established power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dusk square full of people, one phone glowing in the crowd.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the flat-network sentence with a visual of the crowd.
storyboard.addedInformation: The glowing phone in the crowd marks the viral reach of the medium.

left.label: CLINTON CAMPAIGN
left.subject: a formal conference room with a long polished table, a printed flowchart pinned to the wall and staffers in suits seated in rows

right.label: TRUMP NETWORK
right.subject: a loose crowd of ordinary people in a public square, phones raised, no one in charge of the group

storyboard.claim: The 2016 election pitted a rigid hierarchy against a decentralised network.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Left: a formal room with a flowchart on the wall. Right: a loose crowd in a square, phones raised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the battleground into a concrete contrast of structures.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two frames show hierarchy versus decentralised network side by side.

image.subject: a formal conference room with a long polished wooden table, chairs squared neatly, and a large organisation chart framed on the wall

storyboard.claim: The Clinton campaign ran as a rigid traditional hierarchy, the ultimate political tower.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A neat formal room with a long table and an organisation chart on the wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands the left side of the comparison.
storyboard.addedInformation: The organisation chart makes the hierarchy visible.

storyboard.claim: The campaign ran on flowcharts, command chains, vetted messaging and focus groups.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three stacked text items naming the machinery.
storyboard.onScreenText: FLOWCHARTS, CHAIN OF COMMAND, FOCUS GROUPS
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists what the rigid hierarchy consisted of.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the specific tools of the institutional campaign.

image.subject: a stack of printed newspapers on a café table in a city street, a fountain pen resting across the top sheet

storyboard.claim: The old campaign relied on media endorsements, while Trump had a decentralised online network.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Printed newspapers stacked on a café table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the traditional-institutions contrast from the list.
storyboard.addedInformation: Print endorsements stand for the established channel that the network bypassed.

image.subject: a hand holding a glowing smartphone in a dim room, the screen reflecting a blur of faces scrolling past

storyboard.claim: The campaign fed on sheer virality rather than vetting or focus groups.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A hand holding a glowing phone in a dim room, the screen full of faces.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the decentralised network worked.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone screen shows how sharing replaced vetting.

image.subject: a single glowing phone lying face-up on a dark wooden table, beside an untouched stack of old printed books

storyboard.claim: The algorithm cared about engagement, not truth or institutional approval.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A glowing phone beside an untouched stack of old books.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the rule the phone was following.
storyboard.addedInformation: Books left untouched show truth losing to engagement.

image.subject: rows of server racks in a dim data centre, their small status lights blinking across the aisle

storyboard.claim: The more attention a node got, the more it attracted, and outrage was amplified.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Long rows of server racks with blinking lights.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the user's phone to the machinery behind it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The data centre is where the attention feedback loop runs.

image.subject: a tangle of raw data cables spilling from an open junction box in a dark machine room

storyboard.claim: A flood of raw data from outside aided the decentralised network and let it outmanoeuvre the hierarchy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Data cables spilling from an open junction box.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the external shock to the attention loop.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cables stand for the raw data that was pumped into the system.

storyboard.claim: The tower could not move fast enough to counter the square.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-carried statement: the tower and square contrast.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the verdict on the 2016 contrast.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the square as faster than the tower.

storyboard.claim: The square finally beat the tower for good, the flat network's ultimate victory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-carried punchline with no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pays off the tower-versus-square verdict.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the victory the internet was supposed to deliver.

image.subject: a British historian in his fifties, short greying hair, dark sport jacket over an open-collar shirt, seated at a wooden desk with books, looking up earnestly at the camera

storyboard.claim: The host warns against celebrating the network and asks who actually owns it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host at his wooden desk with books, looking up.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from the victory story to a warning.
storyboard.addedInformation: The host's face signals the caution.

storyboard.claim: Look at the physical structure of the internet, not just the web.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-carried question with no picture.
storyboard.onScreenText: WHAT DO YOU MEAN? PHYSICAL INTERNET
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The host's question prompts the physical argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shifts the discussion from the web to its physical base.

left.label: USERS
left.subject: a crowd of ordinary people scattered across a city street, seen from behind, each going their own way

right.label: INFRASTRUCTURE
right.subject: a tight cluster of server racks in a single concentrated data centre hall

storyboard.claim: The users are decentralised, but the infrastructure is not.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Left: scattered people on a street. Right: a tight cluster of server racks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question about physical structure.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts scattered users with concentrated machinery.

image.subject: a coil of fibre-optic cable on a ship's deck at dusk, the grey sea and a distant horizon behind it

storyboard.claim: The physical net is platforms, server farms and fibre-optic cables under the ocean.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A coil of fibre-optic cable on a ship deck with the sea behind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the physical layer after the infrastructure contrast.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the undersea cable as a real object.

image.subject: a grand marble building facade behind a locked iron gate, a single guard standing in front of it, no people admitted

storyboard.claim: These are not public squares owned by the people; they are concentrated corporate towers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A locked iron gate in front of a grand marble building.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Denies the public-square reading of the platforms.
storyboard.addedInformation: The locked gate shows that the square is privately owned.

image.subject: a tall glass corporate tower at night, its windows lit, seen from a quiet city street below

storyboard.claim: The platforms are unequal corporate towers run by small boards.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tall lit glass tower at night seen from the street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows from the locked gate to the tower itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the tower literal in a modern setting.

image.subject: an empty boardroom at night, a long dark table with a few leather chairs pushed back and one lamp lit at the head

storyboard.claim: Small boards of directors, or single CEOs, hold near absolute authority.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty boardroom with one lamp at the head of a long table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes who sits inside the tower.
storyboard.addedInformation: The single lamp at the head shows power concentrated in one seat.

image.subject: Mark Zuckerberg, a 21st-century American tech founder in his thirties, short brown hair, plain grey T-shirt under a dark hoodie, no tie, standing in a dim server hall with one hand resting on a control panel

storyboard.claim: Zuckerberg or Musk can flip a switch and change the flow of information globally.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Zuckerberg in a hoodie with a hand on a control panel in a dim server hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts a named founder at the control panel.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hand on the panel shows the single-switch power.

image.subject: a glass penthouse window high above a city at night, the lights of the streets far below

storyboard.claim: They set the rules of the square from the penthouse of an invisible tower.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A high penthouse window looking down on a dark city.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the single-switch image upward to the tower's top.
storyboard.addedInformation: The view from above shows the square far below the rule-makers.

image.subject: the guarded entrance of a glass office tower, a security guard standing beside the revolving door, ordinary people on the pavement outside

storyboard.claim: The square is being swallowed by the new tower, which is heavily guarded.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A guarded glass entrance with ordinary people outside on the pavement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the tower down to the street-level entrance.
storyboard.addedInformation: The people outside show the square being swallowed.

image.subject: an ordinary person seen from behind at a café window table, a phone in hand, a city street outside the glass

storyboard.claim: We feel like equals in a horizontal network, but we are data points generating ad revenue.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An ordinary person from behind at a café window, phone in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the tower back to the individual user.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the user as the product.

image.subject: an empty cobbled stone square seen from high above, the long shadow of a tower falling across it

storyboard.claim: The illusion of the square masks the reality of the tower.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty cobbled square with a tower's shadow across it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the tower-and-square argument with an image.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shadow shows the tower behind the square.

storyboard.claim: We have tracked the battle between networks and hierarchies across a thousand years.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-carried place card for the long span of history.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pauses the argument to step back.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the whole book's timescale.

image.subject: a magnifying glass resting on an old map of Europe in a candle-lit library, the lens enlarging a faded city

storyboard.claim: The towers-and-squares frame is seductive and makes everything seem to make sense.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A magnifying glass over an old map in a candle-lit library.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Admits the frame's appeal after the step back.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lens image stands for the frame used to read history.

image.subject: a British historian in his fifties, short greying hair, dark sport jacket over an open-collar shirt, seated at a wooden desk with books, a pen in hand, pausing to think

storyboard.claim: The host offers an honest critique of the book's fundamental premise.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host at his desk with a pen, pausing to think.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the admiration to the critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pen and pause show the critical stance.

image.subject: a cracked old map of Europe lying on a desk under a single candle, the paper splitting along its folds

storyboard.claim: The lens has a dangerous flaw when applied too universally and strains under reality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cracked old map under a single candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the flaw using the same map.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cracked map shows the lens breaking under reality.

image.subject: a small wooden box too tight for a heap of handwritten letters and maps spilling over its edges

storyboard.claim: Forcing every connection into the network versus hierarchy box is a massive intellectual risk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A small wooden box overflowing with letters and maps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the flaw shows up in practice.
storyboard.addedInformation: The overflow shows history that does not fit the box.

storyboard.claim: Forcing the frame validates the paranoid style of politics.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-carried question with no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the risk the box creates.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question makes the viewer test the risk.

image.subject: a loose circle of writers in an early 1900s London drawing room, talking and laughing over teacups, seen from behind

storyboard.claim: A messy group of friends in London just talking about art is being equated with conspiracy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Writers in an early 1900s London drawing room over teacups.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the innocent example that the question was about.
storyboard.addedInformation: The teacups and laughter show a harmless social circle.

left.label: PEN PALS
left.subject: an 18th-century man in a long coat writing letters at a candle-lit desk by an open window

right.label: CABAL
right.subject: a shadowy back room with a closed door, a single dim lamp, and a round table with nobody seated

storyboard.claim: Letter-writing friends are being equated with sinister cabals imagined by conspiracy theorists.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Left: a man writing letters by candlelight. Right: an empty round table in a shadowy room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets the innocent example against the conspiracy image.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the two readings of the same network side by side.

image.subject: a pile of handwritten letters on a plain wooden table beside an inkwell and a burning candle

storyboard.claim: Not every network is a conspiracy; sometimes people are just writing letters.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Handwritten letters beside an inkwell and a candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the cabal comparison with the plain fact.
storyboard.addedInformation: The letters are the ordinary object behind the network.

image.subject: a small group of people chatting in an old town square on a sunny day, seen from behind, no one looking at the camera

storyboard.claim: They are chatting in the square, not tunnelling under the tower.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A small group chatting in an old sunny square.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the letters to the people who wrote them.
storyboard.addedInformation: A sunny square makes the innocence of the group visible.

image.subject: an old round wooden table in a dim room, a candle burning down and scattered papers with pencil lines drawn across them

storyboard.claim: Reading history this way turns every listener into an amateur conspiracy theorist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dim round table with a candle and scattered marked-up papers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Warns of the habit the cabal reading creates.
storyboard.addedInformation: The marked papers show a viewer hunting for hidden links.

image.subject: an ordinary person seen from behind at a cluttered kitchen table late at night, papers scattered around, head bowed in one hand

storyboard.claim: Usually it is chaotic, flawed, stressed people making things up as they go and just trying to survive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An ordinary person at a cluttered kitchen table late at night.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the human reality behind the grand plots.
storyboard.addedInformation: The late-night table shows people improvising rather than plotting.

image.subject: a lantern-lit cobbled street at night, a lone figure walking unsteadily through the dark between closed doorways

storyboard.claim: History is more about stumbling through the dark and dealing with unintended consequences.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lone lantern-lit figure on a dark cobbled street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises the human reality into a claim about history.
storyboard.addedInformation: The unsteady figure shows history as improvisation.

storyboard.claim: If the framework is flawed but the history is real, what is the takeaway?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-carried question with no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Asks the question that the final truth answers.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the closing takeaway as a question.

image.subject: a British historian in his fifties, short greying hair, dark sport jacket over an open-collar shirt, seated at a wooden desk with books, leaning forward to speak

storyboard.claim: We are not moving from a dark age of towers into a utopian age of squares.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host at his desk, leaning forward to speak.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the host to deliver the closing structural truth.
storyboard.addedInformation: The forward lean signals the final verdict.
